kitDescription: Leona is a Water Supporter who buffs her team, especially shotgun allies. As she fires, every 5 shots she stacks a small team-wide Critical Rate buff (Roar, up to 5 stacks, 5 seconds each), and every 15 shots she extends the maximum effective range of all shotgun allies for 10 seconds. Whenever the team enters Full Burst she raises all allies' Hit Rate for 10 seconds and grants +5 pellets for 10 seconds to the two highest-final-ATK shotgun allies. Her own Burst II gives the whole team a large Critical Damage buff for 10 seconds, and — when Roar is fully stacked — an additional large Critical Rate buff for shotgun allies only. She has no personal damage mechanics; her entire value is the crit, hit-rate, range, and pellet support she provides to a shotgun-heavy team.

skill1.kitLine: after 5 normal attacks: Roar Crit Rate ▲2.62%, ×5

skill1.formulaCheck: Engine SSOT (sim.ts:2899-2912): the hitCount counter adds hitsPerShot (=10 pellets) PER PULL. count:50 therefore fires on the 5th pull = the kit's '5 normal attacks'; count:5 fires on the FIRST pull (10 ≥ 5) and is exactly the pellet-counting misread S2b named as the nearest-wrong model. The S6 blind's own recipe converges on count:50. The blind agents misread the engine's counter semantics — a RECON_ERROR on their side, not a driver divergence. Driver's L1 pin (first proc after the 4th pull, counterfactual count:5 procs on pull 1) discriminates this correctly.
skill1.explanation: Encoding is correct for this engine's pellet-per-pull counter; generic critRatePct (not critRateNormalPct) matches the unscoped 'Critical Rate' wording; both blinds converged on stat/value/stacks/duration/target. The count:50-vs-count:5 divergence is attributed to the blind side.

verdictRationale: No REAL-GOTCHA exists: every divergence between driver and blinds is either a blind-side recon error or a converged, documented gap. The headline divergence (Roar hitCount count:50 vs count:5) resolves FOR the driver — the engine SSOT adds hitsPerShot=10 per pull, so count:50 is precisely the kit's '5 normal attacks' and count:5 is the pellet-counting misread S2b itself named as nearest-wrong; the S6 blind's own recipe converges on count:50, making this a RECON_ERROR by the blind agents, not a finding. The remaining two approximations (pellet top-2 scope ⚑3, Roar-max gate ⚑4) are documented identically and independently by driver AND blind, both rooted in real schema/engine gaps (no weapon-filter+top-N TargetDef; no buff-stack gate), with honest error directions and measurement recipes rather than fudges. Convergence is strong where it matters: S5's 22 behavioral assertions run GREEN against the shipped override unmodified, and driver + S5 + S6 triple-converged on every stat, value, trigger keying (fullBurstEnter vs burstCast split), and scope — including the pelletCountFlat-5-over-proxy fix the blind derived independently. Discrimination holds: each load-bearing driver pin is paired with a counterfactual that fails it (count:5 first-proc timing, burstCast/fullBurstEnter frame separation, unscoped-target leaks), and S5's cadence band independently rejects pellet-counted Roar. Residual same-model risk for the owner to spot-check: (1) the shared assumption that 'normal attack' = trigger pull rather than pellet for SG hit-count lines — all agents read it the same way, and it is the load-bearing premise behind count:50; (2) whether Roar actually sustains 5 stacks across reloads in game (⚑1 cadence + ⚑4 gate both ride on the unmeasured SG cadence tuple) — if stacks reset each reload, the burst rider is partly dead in game and the override over-credits it; both are flagged with footage recipes, none blocking.
